correctness.rationale: The LCF graph has twelve vertices, eighteen distinct edges and degree three throughout; the defined matching complex has exactly 1,025 nonempty faces with dimension counts (18,117,333,397,152,8). An explicit deterministic staged matching creates 502 disjoint matched codimension-one pairs. The complete 3,629-incidence oriented Hasse graph visits all 1,025 faces in a topological sort, proving that the matching is acyclic. Precisely one dimension-zero and twenty dimension-three faces survive, so finite discrete Morse theory gives a CW model with one zero-cell and twenty three-cells and no intermediate cells; all attaching maps are constant and the homotopy type is a wedge of twenty three-spheres. Standard-library verification was executed against the included program. The independently computed mod-two boundary ranks (17,100,233,144,8) agree but are not used to infer the integral homotopy type.

originality.rationale: The Frucht source specifies the named cubic graph, not the matching-complex topology. The strongest inspected relevant general theorem covers outerplanar graphs only, whereas the Frucht graph is cubic and not outerplanar. Full published result texts for the Frucht independence complex and the Franklin matching complex concern, respectively, a different simplicial-complex construction and a different graph. The searched public mathematical records and literature did not identify a statement implying this exact homotopy classification. This is a best-supported comparison, not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: This gives the full integral homotopy type of the canonical smallest-order asymmetric cubic planar example, a natural benchmark for studying matching-complex topology without automorphism reductions. Its five-dimensional matching complex has a perfect three-dimensional Morse model, a substantial collapse not obvious from its face vector. The exact twenty-sphere rank is an invariant not forced by its cubic degree sequence or the general outerplanar results. The result is useful for separating graph-matching topology from the graph's symmetry structure without asserting a family theorem.
